request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
A few small things came up that might be worth clarifying or tweaking for future games:

1. **Open-cave/blocking ambiguity** — At game turn 53, my status said the way west was “blocked by pirate-3” because Pirate-3 was standing on D1, the now-open cave. Yet `go_to D1` succeeded anyway, because the open cave “holds any number.” That worked out, but the wording was contradictory and could easily make a player hesitate or misplay. It would help if the status line stopped saying a pirate is “blocking” a square once it’s an open cave, or if the rules explicitly said the open cave never blocks movement.

2. **Digging the cave on your final turn means you can’t enter** — `dig` reveals the cave, but `enter` is a separate action on a later turn. So a pirate who discovers the cave on their very last turn would get no bounty at all, which feels punishing for the hero move. Maybe either allow entering on the same turn you dig the cave, or make it clearer how much of a last-turn penalty this is.

3. **The “blocked by pirate” wording during approach** — It’s fine that a pirate in a normal square stops you, but since the open cave exception exists, the rules could state explicitly whether a pirate standing in the open cave still stops a walker before they “enter.” In our game it was resolved in our favor, but the prompt was misleading.

4. **Unshared digs can silently waste crew effort** — In our game everyone shared, but since an unshared `dig` tells only the digger, a single pirate forgetting to share can leave the whole crew re-digging squares. That’s probably intentional, but it’s a sharp punishment for one line of miscommunication in a co-op game.

Overall the reading/triangulation loop worked really well; the main friction was just the open-cave blocker wording.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

One thing the designers should know: there was a confusing edge case when the cave was already open.

At C1, my last turn before entering, the prompt told me:

> "The way east is blocked by pirate-1."

But D1 was already the open cave, and the rules say the open cave “holds any number” of pirates. So it wasn’t clear whether a pirate standing on the open cave should still be considered a blocking obstacle. I gambled that it wouldn’t block, and `go_to D1` worked. If the intended rule is that pirates on an open cave do **not** block movement, then the status line should say something like “pirate-1 is standing on the open cave to the east” rather than “blocked.”

If the intended rule is that a pirate on the cave mouth does still block until they actually use `enter`, then the phrase “holds any number” needs more explanation, because it reads as if the square can contain everyone at once.

Either way, the wording could prevent future crews from hesitating at the final step.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

- Everyone posted their start-square digs and shared the readings.
- We treated each reading as an interval, not an exact number, since the truth could be off by up to 4.
- The final solve was forced from public data: after all shared readings, only C1 and D1 remained. P2 dug and shared C1, it wasn’t the cave, so D1 was the only candidate. I was already on D1 and dug it to open the cave.

If the designers want feedback, one small quirk stood out: a `say` line sent with a `dig` goes out *before* the dig’s result is known, so when I dug D1 I couldn’t truthfully announce “this is the cave!” on that turn. I could only say “if this reveals the cave, come here.” That’s not broken, but it creates a one-turn delay in announcing a discovery.

Also, turn-order and distance can make it mathematically impossible for some pirates to reach the cave even when they correctly deduce it — P4 figured out D1 but had too few turns left. That seems intended by the design, but it’s a real scoring tension the crew has to accept.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
From a design standpoint, a few things stood out:

- **A pirate can become effectively unsalvageable.** P4 was sent to H7 as a probing point while the treasure cluster turned out to be far away. Even after the cave was identified with several turns still on the clock, P4 physically could not reach it in time. The scoring system punishes that even though it was a reasonable crew decision. Designers might want a mechanic to prevent a fully stranded player — e.g., a "move bonus" once the cave is found, or a way to enter from adjacent if the cave is open.

- **Once you commit to a `go_to`, you can’t reroute unless an alert stops you.** When P3 alerted about D1, other pirates could only stop and then rechoose; if no alert had been sent, they would have kept walking toward stale destinations and possibly missed the cave entirely. That makes coordination overly dependent on timing alerts perfectly.

- **The ±4 error is fun for deduction, but the candidate sets can shrink to a tiny cluster.** This made the ending feel like a "dig all candidates one by one" checklist. That's not bad, but it might be more satisfying if probes farther away could still discriminate between close candidates.

- **A very small rules clarification:** a reading "never below 1" could be ambiguous when the treasure is actually on the dug square — a dig at the cave would reveal it, so it probably doesn't matter, but clarifying that readings are only for non-cave squares would be tidy.

Overall the crew coordination and scroll system worked well; the main issue is just the risk of stranding a member who is used for reconnaissance.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
